follow-on: assert applied == pytest.approx(0.30 + 5.40) compares the runner total against the literal spends the test injected into _RecordingDrain, so both sides move with the fixture and it holds whatever the estimate code does.
follow-on: assert result.total_cost == pytest.approx(3.0) compares against the cost_fn constant the test itself injected, so it moves with the fixture rather than an independent source.
follow-on: _DOC_COST_QUERY applies LIMIT $row_cap before grouping by run_id, so a run carrying many LLMCost rows can be truncated mid-run and its run_cost and name list both understated.
